slides.0.title: Cassis, Palette, Bellet and Pierrevert
slides.0.subtitle: Four small appellations, four styles
slides.1.title: Cassis and Palette
slides.1.highlights.0.title: Cassis
slides.1.highlights.0.content: A small port east of Marseille; AOC from 1936 (among France's first), white-led, below the Cap Canaille cliffs
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Palette
slides.1.highlights.1.content: A tiny appellation near Aix, AOC 1948; Château Simone is emblematic, with 20-plus permitted varieties led by Mourvèdre, Grenache and Cinsault
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Common thread
slides.1.highlights.2.content: Both are small, traditional zones hemmed in by urban areas
slides.1.content: Small zones with strong character.
slides.2.title: Bellet
slides.2.highlights.0.title: Above Nice
slides.2.highlights.0.content: Hills behind Nice, AOC 1941, extremely small
slides.2.highlights.1.title: Local varieties
slides.2.highlights.1.content: White centres on Rolle (Vermentino); red uses Braquet and Folle Noire (Fuella)
slides.2.highlights.2.title: Italian roots
slides.2.highlights.2.content: Close to Italy, its varieties share roots with Liguria and Piedmont
slides.2.content: A local-grape enclave behind Nice.
slides.3.title: Pierrevert
slides.3.highlights.0.title: Northern highlands
slides.3.highlights.0.content: In the Durance valley of Alpes-de-Haute-Provence, higher and cooler at night
slides.3.highlights.1.title: Style
slides.3.highlights.1.content: Fresher, lighter reds, whites and rosés, between Provence and the Rhône
slides.3.highlights.2.title: Position
slides.3.highlights.2.content: Not coastal; an inland highland complement
slides.3.content: High and cool: Provence's northern edge.
